summary: This tutorial explains storage class specifiers in C programming, specifically focusing on `auto` and `static`. The `auto` keyword indicates automatic storage duration, meaning variables have local scope and must be initialized before use; otherwise, the compiler will throw an error if they are not. An example demonstrates this by declaring an `auto` variable `i` within a function, which must be initialized to avoid errors. The `static` keyword, on the other hand, also has local scope but retains its value between function calls, allocated in CPU memory. An example shows initializing a `static` variable `i` to zero, which persists across multiple function calls, resulting in an output of zero when printed.
